question: Which country's President suggested the name "United Nations"?
solution:
The correct answer is__** the United States of America**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **name "United Nations" was suggested by United States President** Franklin Delano Roosevelt.
 
• The **term was first used in the Declaration **by the United Nations on January 1, 1942, during World War II.
 
• The** declaration was signed by representatives of 26 nations **who pledged to continue fighting together against the Axis Powers. 
 
• The name was **unanimously adopted at the San Francisco Conference as a tribute to the late President.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The United Nations (UN) is an international organization founded on 24th October 1945.
 
• Its Headquarters is in New York, United States.
 
• The present Secretary-general is Antonio Guterres.
 
• It has 193 Member States and 2 observer states.
 
• It has 6 official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish
